changes: First rent, but small: 18 critical IT MW delivered at Black Pearl and $5.9mn of HPC lease revenue; mining was still 78% of revenue, so total revenue missed consensus by about 31%.

Cipher issued a ready-for-service notice for Barber Lake's first 51 critical IT MW (call only; not yet rent). Cost is now about $13.0mn per IT MW against $10.4mn financed; management puts average yield on cost back at 15.2% only with the 20-year lease (12.9% without it).
Management said early leases were rushed on immature designs. New leases wait for 30% to 60% design completion and are priced on yield on cost, which slows signing: no new campus lease since March.

Shares rose 9.9% in a month (415.1mn at 30 September to 456.4mn at 30 October) on the convert exchange, and the 10-Q still names at-the-market sales as a liquidity source. Pro forma unrestricted cash and bitcoin is $724mn.

Not asked on the call: Google's warrants carry a $435mn value test when the Fluidstack lease commences. At about $6.93 the 26.2mn warrant shares are worth about $182mn, so a shortfall of roughly $250mn would be owed in shares or cash [our approximate arithmetic; how value is measured is not disclosed].
Project notes marked down: 10-Q fair values fell to 100.5, 97.9 and 95.6 of par at 30 September from 104.2, 101.5 and 100.4 at 30 June.
checks: A fresh subagent checked the draft against the 8-K, deck, release, both 10-Qs, the transcript extract and the price article: about 150 figures and claims confirmed, six wording or attribution errors fixed, and derived figures recomputed in code (25% cost rise, 9.9% shares, 3Q capex and OCF as 9M less H1, ex-warrant net income -$95.6mn reconciling to -$0.22, fair values as percent of par). Open: warrant share count is approximate (24.18mn plus about 2.0mn; EPS tables show 24.7mn), the floor is $435mn in the 3Q 10-Q but $430mn in 2Q, and the valuation method and trigger for a phased commencement are undisclosed. Call items rest on extracts of an AI-assisted Investing.com transcript, not raw text. Consensus varies by provider ($37.49mn to $38.69mn); the miss holds on all. No bond quote after 30 September found.
consensus_thesis: Investors own Cipher as a Texas build-to-suit landlord whose 700 gross MW of backstopped or investment-grade leases turn into rent as halls are delivered, while pricing heavy doubt about build cost, dilution and parent funding.
headline: The contracted-rent view holds but should move from 'overruns are a one-off' to 'returns were preserved by a longer lease and parent cash': Barber Lake's cost rose 25% to about $13.0mn per IT MW, 41mn new shares followed, no new campus lease was signed, and long-term credit quality holds rather than improves until halls bill on schedule.
kona: Management's own account is the lesson: leases signed on immature designs cost Cipher 25% on build cost, and the hyperscaler leases with capex allowances passed overruns to the tenant while the modified-gross Fluidstack lease passed on only half of costs above the first $359.3mn. Kona should freeze design to at least 30% before signing and write a capex allowance into any lease. Rents are reportedly moving with financing costs, so Kona should quote on yield on cost (Barber Lake's achieved figure is about 15%; no target was stated) rather than a fixed $/kW-month. On-site gas is converging on an independent power producer that sells to the tenant under a PPA, with yields in line with grid sites, and Cipher targets gas in 2027 and about 1 GW of talks, so Kona's off-grid edge must rest on speed and gas cost, not on the model being unusual.
monitor: MW billing at 31 December by site, against 18 MW today and the 51 MW Barber Lake notice; first Barber Lake rent in the 4Q release.
ERCOT final Batch Zero classification for Colchis in December, and any signed lease at Reveille, Ulysses or Odessa, with its funding mix.
Parent cash after remaining Barber Lake funding, at-the-market use below $10, and how the Google warrant shortfall is settled at Fluidstack lease commencement.

sections.body: Trevor's watch-list. No analyst was named by CK; I chose Brett Knoblauch (Cantor), who pressed hardest on cost, though on two quarters and one transcript the choice is thin. 3Q question: when were Barber Lake costs locked in? Answer: rushed leases, immature design, scope, labor, lead times; the lock-in date was not given. Rating: partial. Later evidence: EAC at the next 10-Q. Wider point: nobody asked about the backstop for years 11-20, remaining Barber Lake equity, convert puts or project coverage, even with the stock down sharply. 3Q Q&A is from the Investing.com transcript; 2Q topics are from a Nasdaq call summary, so the 2Q column is partial. — Trevor
